summary:
Scope: capturing a backlog of Claude Code transcripts through the passive path (coord 0.113/0.114 engine, Host 0.9.0 receiver) after the retirement design in github/passive-capture-finite-state-retirement. Measured in October 2026 on one fdev workspace; code constants are in the cited sources and may change, so re-read them before reuse.

Limits that shaped the run: a capture pass scans with a budget of 24 minus the events already in the batch (SkillTelemetryAdapter), so a batch holds about 23 or 24 observations, not the larger figure first estimated; one ready file drains per pass and applying took two drain passes (durably-received, then applied); the producer keeps at most 256 response identities (a pass that would exceed it defers with response-index-full-capture-deferred, and the cursor is retained); an active Claude source keeps its newest 24 completed responses until it reaches a line-boundary end and stays unmodified for the 900 s quiet period, then retires; long-lived sources hold their entries until retired.

Findings: (1) small-files-first ordering does not limit concurrency, because one pass advances every selected file, so each round can activate another source and retained identities rise by up to 24 per source; the peak for N concurrent files is about 24 times N plus whatever other sources hold. A Codex rollout that held 144 entries blocked headroom until one capture of that rollout alone read its last record and retired it (retained 217 to 73). (2) Choose stop thresholds from the peak, not from the batch count: a stop of about 235 against the 256 cap with 8-file selections was never reached once the Codex entries were released. (3) The rate was about one batch per 30 s round, so a backlog of roughly 11.5k identities needed about 450 rounds; budget rounds and a per-day receipt limit from that, not from observations per batch. (4) The dashboard unassigned list truncates at 256, so completeness evidence must be a store count compared with an independent recomputation of identities, never the dashboard. Pattern that held: foreground loop, one batch in flight, controls checked before and after every round, stop on any non-zero exit, rejected receipt, gap name or hash drift. Alternatives such as a separate Claude producer or raising the 256 cap are proposals, not done or admitted. Identity and turn derivation: see github/claude-transcript-native-usage.
title: Claude backlog capture is bounded by 24 events per pass, 256 retained identities and per-source retention; pace one batch at a time
